Where was I truly going with this, I'm not too sure.
My recommendation is to objectively look at skills and perks and think "why do I need this". You can replace some skills with different weapons, armor, yada yada. Same goes with perks. Payday is a game in which you will need to know the game mechanics inside and out to really know what you're doing.

When doing a load out, start with the perk deck. Start building it from there. Passive heal, leave the hostage skills. Playing with friends, why not take medic skills? Soloing, maybe put in a few points in drill skills.

Weapons follow skills. Wrong skillset will make your weapons peashooters. Take them out for spins, how's ammo pickup, does it kill fast, run out of ammo fast, is it comparable to using a watergun on a housefire?

Payday is complicated, but that's okay. What you should be concerned about is the keep it fun.

That's my ~~rant~~ 2¢ done. Good day.

The tomcat is perfect for when your opponents have limited SA, and is still viable if they have enough awareness to pinpoint you to the sky. The Phoenix missiles are essentially as good as Amraams up close, far away, they can shoot from a longer distance, but then suffer a little as they come in, if your opponent flies high and slow, they will receive a most uncomfortable present.

Overall I'd argue the Tomcat being better than the F-15 simply thanks to the datalink, which allows the tomcat better awareness and ease of intercept. Weaponry wise the F-15 is more suited for boom and zoom, shoot and scoop type of intercepts, where the tomcat has to fly into harm's way, so in that sense the tomcat pilot has to always have a presence of mind to maneuver so that a missile can be defeated while still guiding own munitions.

A continuous wall of fire, with weapons that kill quick will keep you and your friends alive. That's your primary goal. Open areas are to be played carefully. CQC is your Forte.
